title: Worst Hop
similar: LeetCode 543 Diameter of Binary Tree (weighted, general tree)
hints: Any longest path has a highest node, the one closest to the root. What does the path look like from that node's point of view?
From a node v the path goes down into at most two different child subtrees. If you knew, for every child, the longest downward path starting at that child, what would you combine?

down[v] = max over children c of down[c] + w(c). The best path with top node v is the sum of the two largest values of (down[c] + w(c)) (or one, or zero). Because every parent index is smaller than its child's, process nodes from n-1 down to 0 and you need no recursion. Use long long.

wrong.through_root.cpp: only considers paths through the root (the deepest two branches of node 0)
wrong.int_overflow.cpp: keeps path sums in 32-bit int, which overflows on long heavy chains
wrong.tle_all_pairs.cpp: runs a traversal from every node (fails the perf group)

strategy.question: Scout the statement: a rooted tree of up to 2*10^5 services with edge latencies up to 10^9; find the largest total latency between any two services. Which plan fits?
options: Run a shortest-path search from every node and take the maximum
Only look at the two deepest branches under the root
One bottom-up pass: for each node keep the best downward path, and combine its two best child branches
Sort the edges by latency and add the largest ones
strategy.why: Searching from every node is O(n^2), far too slow at 2*10^5. The best path need not pass through the root. Summing the largest edges ignores that the edges must form one connected path. A bottom-up pass looks at each node once, using the two best child branches, so it is O(n).
